utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I established that Mr. Markac has not appeared in the courtroom this morning, which has happened before at housekeeping sessions. Before we start with that housekeeping session, Mr. Registrar, would you please -- let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We went into private session at a moment where we had established that Mr. Markac is not present in court today, where a housekeeping session is held. The Markac Defence explained the reasons why Mr. Markac is not present in court and has requested that we would continue with the housekeeping session, which we'll now do. The housekeeping sessions, apart from a lot of other items on the agenda will also include, but we're not going to start with that, to reduce the size of our MFI list. We start with the Markac submission of an expert report. The expert report was filed on the 9th of October, expert report of Nikica Baric. OTP has objected on the 9th of November. There were no objections from the Gotovina Defence. There were no -- I think there were no other filings. The matter is that Mr. Baric was not called as an expert, which, for admission of his expert report, would have been required under Rule 94 bis, where the opposing party has not accepted the report and has expressed a wish to cross-examine Mr. Baric but he was never called. Under those circumstances, should we declare the submission of the Baric report moot, or is it withdrawn? What would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The submission was withdrawn, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The submission was withdrawn. Then I may have missed that. When was that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As we informed the OTP but I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, usually the Chamber would like to know whether a matter on which it is supposed to decide whether it is withdrawn or not. But now you formally withdraw --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the submission of the expert report of Nikica Baric, pursuant to Rule 94 bis as it was filed on the 9th of October, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's now on the record. The second item on my agenda is Cermak's motion for admissions of documents into evidence, the Bijeljina murders. They have been submitted from the bar table. I would like to know whether there is any objection against having them admitted but I'm -- I saw that the comments of the Office of the Prosecution are included in the established bar table format.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Mr. President. And, in any event, just to make it clear, we do not have any objections to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from any of the other parties. Then the documents were filed -- the motion was filed on the 8th of December of this year [sic]. I have no further -- numbers have not been assigned yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please assign numbers to the documents which were filed. Once the numbers have been assigned, the Chamber will decide to admit into evidence these Bijeljina documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the technical better way is to wait until they have numbers but the decision is there and we will put, then, the numbers on the record. Mr. Registrar, is it clear which documents we are talking about to you? They have been uploaded in e-court, and there was a bar table submission filed on the 8th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's in Annex A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Annex A to that ... yes. Then we move on to the next item on the agenda which is a matter in relation to D420. D420 is already admitted into evidence, but we have the following problem. It is the report on the implementation of the plan of return and care of refugees and displaced persons. The problem is that we have two originals. We have three versions of this document. We have a B/C/S original, 3D00-1242; we have an English original, 3D06-0100, and the two are not exactly the same; and we have what is called an additional translation, which is 3D06-0604. It's clear that D420, which was admitted through Mr. Galbraith, that what appears as an English version, or an English translation is not the same document. Has this matter been further discussed between the parties so that we know what the evidence is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't believe the matter was further discussed, but the issue, as Your Honour has expressed, is that it is not an exact translation. So it's not like we have one document that is the guiding document or the reference and then a document based on that initial source. What we have is two independent documents, although relating the same topic and saying roughly the same things, are not identical. What we would submit is that because the versions are not identical, and we had to obviously look at the English version, that the English document be considered the main exhibit in fairness to us, since that is the one that we reviewed. We did not make an exhaustive line-by-line comparison of the two documents because it is -- they are quite long documents, and it's not clear if there were any substantial differences. But to the extent that in preparation for examination and cross-examination of witnesses we rely on the English version, we would ask that that one be the one that is -- the one that is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, then, to do with the uploaded additional translation, which is now part of D420 as well? Should we strike that or could I hear from the other parties, what -- I mean, the Chamber, of course, is not going to accept in any way that we have additional translations where there's no original from where it was translated. If the English version would do, if that would give the -- then, first of all, we would have to check whether this has any impact on the testimony given by Mr. Galbraith; I have not checked that yet. But, of course, if we have to understand his testimony in relation to this document, then, of course, it should be clear what the document is, unless the differences between the two versions of the document are irrelevant for the testimony. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we haven't given this much thought because we didn't know this was on the agenda for today. But the -- what comes to my mind is that the document wasn't only put to Mr. Galbraith but it was also put to Mr. Pejkovic who would have reviewed the document in the Croatian version. So it may be the best solution is simply to have both documents become exhibits, the Croatian with the translation, which I presume is the translation of the Croatian original, and then if the Prosecution wishes to rely on the English, they can tender it as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have, as a matter of fact, we do not have a full translation, I think. Let's have D420.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, we don't, Your Honour, because it was a 60 -- 60-some odd page document which was why Your Honour had commented that it may not be -- I think that's why the Defence, when they tendered it, because they had an English version just tendered both of them, although it wasn't a formal translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently the additional English translation, I do not know exactly what it translates. It's 18 pages and -- is there any way that the parties could just sit together and see what should be -- and otherwise we would need either partial translation or a full translation of the B/C/S document to the extent that it does not -- it is not the same as the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I think that we can do that. In deference to Mr. Hedaraly's point, I mean, it could have been that a certain section was used in cross-examination of Ambassador Galbraith, and certainly I understand why counsel would want that in, and yet a revised version was used with somebody else. So I think we just need to go back to the transcripts and take a look at how it was used, and I think we can come to a consensus on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It appears that there's great willingness to resolve the matter and not to make it a subject of eternal dispute. The Chamber will wait and see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next point on my agenda, and we referred to it briefly -- no, I -- the next point on my agenda is the MFI list. The MFI list has been distributed to the parties, from what I understand. The first one is D215, which is a document which was admitted into evidence. The problem was that it was not fully translated. The -- D215 was used with witnesses, I think, Galbraith and Gojanovic, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise. Just to interrupt, we received an MFI list. That document is not on the list that -- it is on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We have the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't if we're dealing with two different lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: D1719 is the first one that we received in the documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- marked for identification. I think there may have been other issues but they were not documents marked for identification. So those are the ones that we were preparing for, based on the list that we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the problem is that I have an MFI list on which appear also documents which are not MFIs anymore but where there's still an outstanding matter. I'll move through them. I'll point out what the remaining problem is, although it has already been admitted. I apologise for the confusion created by this. D215, there was an issue of complete or incomplete translation and admission in its totality. That was the problem which was raised earlier, and the Chamber would like to hear the parties' position on the incomplete translation and the fairness of what should be admitted into evidence, what should not have been admitted into evidence. I'll leave it to that for the time being. The next one is also one which was admitted into evidence. That is the ICRC booklet, which was not fully translated. Only one page is there in English. I went through the booklet again yesterday and saw that many, many pages are nice drawings of all kind of situations. Sometimes little text. However, there seems to be text dealing with international humanitarian law as well, which might be worthwhile to have translated. But one of the issues raised by the Chamber is whether there was an English version of this same booklet and whether the parties would try to find an English version, because the ICRC, of course, is not exclusively an organisation working in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will certainly look for it, Mr. President, but if we could ask for an exhibit number so that we can follow with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: D533, I think, is that the one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D533, yes. And what the Chamber would prefer is that the parties would agree on what portions would be in need of being translated, if no translation yet exists of the text written in that booklet. And I think all the instructions on what to do with someone who is wounded in manner A, or manner B, that speaks for itself, more or less, that these are instructions for care to be given to wounded people, and I don't think that that's -- that we need full translations of that. So could the parties please sit together and see what portions of D533 need to be translated. Then ... I have one more, which also seems to be a document which was already -- could -- there must a little problem with the French booth. I love to hear French, but ... Which in relation to D1791, again, it does not appear on your list, to 1794, that is intelligence findings review for certain periods. And the Chamber has asked the Markac Defence why portions were redacted. You indicated, Mr. Mikulicic, that you would verify and later that you were working on it. Still the matter has not been fully resolved as to why certain portions are missing. I earlier indicated that if the document is not complete that the Chamber might find itself in a situation where it has to reconsider the admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we asked for some explanation according to your guidance but we didn't receive any answer until today. So we will simply try to do it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When was the last time that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the court session where this documents has been introduced. And I -- I cannot remember. I think it was in the mid of November, or in the beginning of the November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And have you, at a later moment, urged for a quick response?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. But we will do it immediately, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is evidence that was introduced by you, and since we are coming closer and closer to the end of the case, Mr. Mikulicic, it really is an urgent matter, and the Chamber would like to receive at least some provisional indication of what we could expect, well, let's say, within the next -- until Monday noon, try to -- perhaps to make telephone contact or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will do our best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we're back on your list. D1719, which is portions of the Jarnjak interview. It was tendered. Then the Prosecution indicated what it needed as context for the tendered parts. And then, on the 16th of November, the tendering was withdrawn. The Chamber -- it was all about the way in which interviews took place. It was meant to be an illustration of what happened and not that much the content of the Jarnjak interview itself but -- The Chamber is -- was considering but we'll give you the decision on whether the Chamber would like to have this -- these portions of the interview in evidence, although it was not tendered anymore by the Gotovina Defence. The Chamber will inform you about it, if possible today. Then I move on to D1877, up to and including D1882, which are Cermak Defence bar table submissions. It is related to the cross-examination of Mr. Moric. The bar table submission was filed on the 18th of December in the required format. There seem to be no objections. Is it entirely clear from the format whose comments are in this comments table? May I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They're agreed comments, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They're agreed comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- and they have been circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They have been circulated. No, it is just that these are agreed comments, because often we find OTP comments on it, but these are agreed comments. In the absence of any objection then, D1877, up to and including D1882, are admitted into evidence. I move on to -- the Gotovina bar table submissions, D1883, up to and including D1892. The Chamber was informed on the 7th of December that an agreement had been reached between the Gotovina Defence and the Prosecution; more specifically, Ms. Mahindaratne. On the 9th of December, the bar table submission was MFI'd in court. If there are no objections, and it appears that there are none, the Chamber will decide on -- no, let me just ... I think the bar table was -- the submissions -- is this part of the omnibus bar table --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, it was not. It was separate and apart of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Could you tell us exactly when it was filed --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday. That may cause some of my confusion. Although I think I have seen ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it assists, it was circulated at 5.03 p.m. by the court ushers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have now the filing before me. What we see is that D1883, up to and including D1892, which are mostly reports on on-site MUP investigations of the second half of August 1995, and one cover letter with correspondence in which Mr. Kardum passes instructions from the Moric to the police administration to do on-site investigations. All to do with on-site investigations. They have now been presented -- they have all been presented now in the format which the Chamber requires. There seems to be no further comments from the Prosecution. Is there any comments from any of the other parties? No objections. Therefore, D1883, up to and including D1892, are admitted into evidence. Yes, it was included in an e-mail which I was supposed to have read this morning. The matter has been resolved. We move on to the -- we move on to the next one, which is P2640, minutes of a presidential meeting, 11th of April, 1995. Apparently there was some translations issues there. They appear to have been resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Both -- there was both a translation issue and a contextual issue. They both have been resolved and agreed with my learned colleague, Mr. Cayley. So it is ready to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the correct versions have been uploaded meanwhile, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that was -- the Chamber was informed about this on the 18th of November. And, therefore, nothing opposes admission into evidence anymore of this document. P2640 is admitted into evidence. The next one is P2643, which is among -- if I could call them the Skegro documents. Because Mr. Skegro sent us some other documents as well, which were related to this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, I think -- I think there were two separate issues. The documents that Mr. Skegro sent were with respect to a separate allegation that were made by some media reporters. This one was an article in the Independent, and -- who referenced -- which referenced a Presidential transcript which the Prosecution did not have. Based on Your Honours' guidance we have now asked for that Presidential transcript, we have received it, to provide further context. It is in translation now. We were informed we should have it by the -- hopefully the end of the day. So as soon as we have it, we will circulate that and then that exhibit can be considered with its contextual -- with the source of the article and then be moved in together. And then the other issue are the issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, are the six documents sent by Mr. Skegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the original already been disclosed to the -- to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you receive it, Mr. Hedaraly?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I forget, Your Honour. There was back and forth because we -- initially we didn't get it from the Croatian government. We had to go back to them. We are waiting for it to be translated. We received it not too long ago but we can send the B/C/S version right away, or as I said, we should have the translation by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes it allows already a party to look at the document, if they received the original even if it's not yet translated, because parties may have their own means of obtaining access to the content of a document. So, therefore, Mr. Hedaraly, it certainly would have been better to have it disclosed immediately. Any further comments on the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. We have the other Skegro documents, as Your Honour knows, to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the judgements and the -- yes. But as far as this matter is concerned, would we wait and see when the translation is there, and would we then -- I take it that you, Mr. Hedaraly, you want, then, to tender the transcript as directly related to and either corroborating, or not corroborating, the press article.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we have a more -- that we have the better evidence on the matter, and that before the Chamber decides on the matter, that we'll hear from the Cermak Defence whether there are any objections against either the transcript itself or selection translated. And you already provide the original without further delay to the Defence. Mr. Kay, we'll then hear at a later stage knowing what the Prosecution intends to do with this transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And what we intend to do when we get the materials ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now, about the other Skegro documents, I do understand that you have submitted them for translation. I think there were four judgements and there were some -- two more documents. Have you received translation, and have you made up your mind as to what to do with them, if anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's all been distributed. Those documents we now ask to be given exhibit numbers. The Court has been provided with the information. They are the 65 ter numbers 2D00811 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then up to and including --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They've all been disclosed. They went to an issue of his credibility. The documents have been translated, and we ask that they be assigned exhibit numbers and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I find this, including the 65 ter numbers, in your -- in your yesterday's e-mail of 5.30 p.m., where --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see that there are the -- these are P1, P2, T1, R1, as you call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We also link them to the transcript for the Court for ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that all the transcript pages are included in your yesterday e-mail. I think the e-mail in itself, although of assistance to the Court, doesn't add anything so it doesn't have to get any official status. It's just for us, for our information. Then could I hear from the other parties, whether there's any objections against the four documents just mentioned; that is 65 ter 2D00811, up to and including 65 ter 2D00814.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. I hear of no objections from the other Defence teams. Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 2D00811 would receive ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would receive Exhibit D1954. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1954. The next one, last three digits 812.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will receive Exhibit D1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, last three digits 813.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will receive Exhibit D1956. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, finally, the last one, last three digits 814.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will receive Exhibit D1957. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1954, up to and including D1957, are admitted into evidence. The next one on my list is P2644. A decision on admission was already taken, but the -- we are waiting for a new translation. We were informed on the 14th of December by the OTP that a revised translation was uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct. And it was circulated. And it was -- there were no further -- there was no further concerns by the Defence with respect to the revised translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that P2644, which was already admitted into evidence, now is accompanied by a revised translation in e-court. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just noting that in e-court itself the revised translation has not been uploaded, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I must say that on the 14th of December, it said that a revised translation was to be uploaded and -- well, since then it is more than a month, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, I think, Your Honour, that the new procedure is that Mr. Registrar waits to get the approval of the Chamber before himself uploading it. That's why it's ready. It's agreed upon. It's just a matter of formally uploading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so then I have to address Mr. Registrar. Mr. Registrar, have you -- do you have the revised translation in -- available for uploading it and attaching it to the original of P2644?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do. All I need is your instruction to do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have received my instruction about this. Yes, now I remember that the parties are not allowed just to attach new translations without a proper decision, especially if a document is already -- is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't think it was admitted; I think it was MFI'd, Your Honours. You can also have a -- I have it on the MFI list and the status showed up as MFI, so if we can also admit it into evidence formally, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. You're right. I made a mistake. Therefore, P2644 with the newly uploaded translation into English with the approval of the Court is now admitted into evidence. I am now at P2662; extracts from a book by Mate Granic. Prosecution has tendered 14 pages. The pending issue was that the other parties would still be in a position to tender additional relevant portions of the book. Is there any wish to do so? If not, then nothing opposes the admission of P2662, as tendered by the Prosecution, a selection of 14 pages, English version of the book, and, therefore, P2662 is admitted into evidence. P2678, there was a translation issue. The Chamber received, on the 14th of December, a message that the translation issue had been resolved, that the translation was verified, and that the Gotovina Defence finally agreed with the translation as it was then uploaded. Therefore, it seems that nothing opposes admission into evidence anymore. The verification has not resulted in any changes for which I would have to give approval then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: All I know is that there was a revised translation. I don't know if there were any -- I haven't looked into whether any specific changes were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's important to know whether the translation which we have in e-court now is the verified and agreed upon translation as we're talking about. Is this -- could this be verified at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We will check, Your Honour, and we will get back to the Court shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that it is not yet admitted into evidence but we will soon hear and finally decide the matter. Then ... there was an issue in relation to P2604. P2604 was admitted into evidence, and two pages, apparently, were missing, and the OTP has requested these pages to be added. From what I do understand, Ms. Gustafson, you suggested that -- or you initially wanted to add 65 ter 7524 to P2604 but there were some formatting problems. There were also illegibility problems in relation to those documents. At the same time, the Gotovina Defence did not oppose against at least having 65 ter 7524 into evidence, whereas the other Defence teams remained silent on the matter. Are we yet at a point that perhaps 65 ter 7524 could be assigned a separate exhibit number, although it is related to P2604. Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's -- in light of the different formats and different nature of the translations of the two documents, perhaps it's best that it actually be assigned a separate number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will deliver a decision on this transcript. However, in view of the confusion that came up in relation to page numbers, et cetera, the Chamber would like to first verify, in a short break later this morning, whether any reference to page numbers, whether we would have similar mistakes. We just want to verify that before I read that decision from the Chamber. But the Chamber has made up its mind as to what is still to be done and what is not to be done anymore, in relation to the Brioni transcript. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to the translation of D970; also in relation to P1272, if I say "udar" or "udare," everyone will immediately know what we are talking about. The Chamber has considered what to do, under the present circumstances, where a further explanation and verification has been sought by CLSS, and where the Gotovina Defence has put on the record that it was still not satisfied with this explanation and the translation. The Chamber has considered that in full awareness of the continuing dispute that the Chamber will evaluate this portion of the evidence with great caution and in -- and as part of the entirety of the evidence but will not take further action at this moment and leaves the matter for the time being as it is. But as I said before, the Chamber is aware of the dispute, the not finally yet settled dispute on the translation. Then I'd like to read out a decision, in relation to reasons for granting protective measures to Witness MM-025. On the 3rd of December, 2009, the Markac Defence requested the Chamber to grant Witness MM-025 the protective measures of pseudonym as well as voice and image distortion. On the 4th of December, the Markac Defence filed a corrigendum, requesting to have the testimony of the witness delivered in closed session. On the 15th of December, 2009, the Prosecution objected to the request. And this can be found on transcript page 26.274. On the same day, the Chamber heard directly from Witness MM-025 about the reasons for the requested protective measures and subsequently granted the request, with reasons to follow. This decision can be found at transcript page 26.291 and the public is hereby informed of it. The Chamber has previously held that a party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that the witness has given evidence before this Tribunal. This standard can, for example, be satisfied by showing that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family. Even though the granting of protective measures is, and should be, the exception to the rule of a public trial, the threshold for when it should be granted cannot be set too high. For example, to exclude persons who have not experienced threats and harassment would defy the purpose of the measures; namely, protection for risks that might occur as a result of the testimony. The Chamber must therefore make a risk assessment, and inherent in such an assessment is applying a certain level of caution and erring on the safe side. Witness MM-025 was intermittently a member of the SVK between 1991 and 1995, and was allegedly mistreated in the Republika Srpska. A family member of the witness was killed under unknown circumstances. The witness was expected to testify about an event which may identify him with the community in which he currently lives and works. After 1995, the witness returned to Croatia, where he lives with his family, while part of his family lives in Serbia. Giving testimony is not looked upon favourably by some people the witness encounters in his work. In the context of his work, for which the witness travels within the territory of the former Yugoslavia, the witness has also been called Ustasha. For the foregoing reasons, the witness feared that, should it become known that he had testified, the security and welfare of both his family and himself may be put at risk. Having considered all of the above, the Chamber found that the Markac Defence had demonstrated an objectively grounded risk that, should it become known that Witness MM-025 has given evidence before this Tribunal, it would place the security and welfare of the witness and his family at risk. The Chamber furthermore considered that, in light of the nature of the anticipated evidence of the witness, the only effective way to protect his identity was to hear his testimony in closed session. This concludes the Chamber's reasons for its decision to grant protective measures to Witness MM-025. I move on. The next item on my list is Markac's motion to amend its 65 ter witness list. It is a matter which is to some extent already in the past, because the witness has testified already, Ms. Bagic. Has the corrigendum been filed of the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move on to -- let me just have a look. Mr. Registrar, I would like to invite you to tell us whether you have received any communication by the parties which would possibly result in changes in uploaded documents, replacements of translations, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can assist, Your Honour, there are a -- there a number of such documents. There's P604 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I previously discussed with the Registrar that he had a short list of where he received matters which he cannot further proceed with without the approval of the Chamber, and, therefore, I invited him to give the -- to list them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we dealt with P604 and P2644. Then we have an outstanding issue in relation to D1392, where the -- where we need pages 36 and 37 to be uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the technical difficulty has been fixed. Let me then go back to where we were. I was just saying that there was a problem in relation to D1392, where pages 36 and 37 were still to be uploaded and to have them inserted into this exhibit which needs the approval of the Chamber. Any further observations or submissions in relation to this? If not, Mr. Registrar, you're instructed to have pages 36 and 37, doc ID 3D06-1461 to be inserted in D1392.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is just -- I'm sorry. There was -- one small observation is that these two pages are not simply the missing pages. They are a translation of the B/C/S original of those two pages and they correspond - we've looked at it - but just so that they're not simply two pages that were missing and found later. They were found from the B/C/S version which was not in evidence, which was not linked, and these portions were translated and inserted in their place. Just wanted to make sure that is on the record, so that we don't think it's simply two pages missing and they were found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Relying on this information and to be quite honest it rings a bell but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I'm informed that actually the two original English pages were found and were circulated this morning. And Mr. Registrar has actually the original English missing pages, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The information on which I relied was from the 18th of January, so this is new information, because I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This morning it was e-mailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This morning it was e-mailed. Mr. Hedaraly, just as I was happy to rely on you, would you rely on Mr. Misetic's information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I would rely on it, if he would be so kind -- we'll look at it just to make sure, but that's -- we'll rely on that, and I'm sure Mr. Registrar also has the same ones. But we will obviously double-check, and if we have any concerns, we will raise them; but I don't think it will be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, yes, the Registrar is instructed to add the pages 36 and 37, as requested by the Gotovina Defence in its today's e-mail at 8.56. Mr. Registrar, is this sufficient information for you?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the next one is D680, which is about a revised translation amended to Articles 1 and 3. Apparently there's no objection from the Prosecution. Mr. Registrar, you're instructed to replace the translation as it is found now in e-court by the revised translation, as provided by the OTP. Then I'd like to deliver a statement concerning the Brioni transcripts, as I announced before. The Chamber would now like to deliver a decision concerning the Gotovina Defence 's submission regarding Exhibit P461, which is the Brioni transcript, filed on the 1st of April, 2009. In the submission, the Gotovina Defence challenged the accuracy of P461, pointing out three categories of mistakes. The first category pertains to several audible portions of the Brioni meeting that allegedly were not transcribed correctly or were not transcribed at all. The second category pertains to passages of the transcript that allegedly have been attributed to wrong speakers. The third category refers to alleged errors in the translation of the transcript. The Gotovina Defence attached to its submission a revised version of the transcript, the transcript currently in evidence as P461, and a table singling out, according to the Gotovina Defence, the differences between the two. The Prosecution responded on the 15th of April, 2009, only agreeing to four changes and objecting to the rest of the Gotovina Defence's version of the transcript. According to the Prosecution, some changes are minor and irrelevant; others cannot be verified without the help of a witness familiar with the conduct of the meeting, the voices of the alleged speakers, or both. According to the Prosecution, the Gotovina Defence failed to provide any source for its proposed changes. The Prosecution concluded that, if the Chamber considers any of the changes proposed by the Gotovina Defence and not agreed to by the Prosecution, to be relevant to any substantive issue in this case, the relevant parts of the transcript should be submitted for independent transcription and/or interpretation, as applicable. With regard to the missing or otherwise incorrectly transcribed parts of the Brioni meeting, the Chamber has selected a number of passages amongst the ones pointed out by the Gotovina Defence. The Chamber directs the Gotovina Defence to extract these passages from the original audio of the meeting and submit them to CLSS for transcription and translation. I'm asking now specific attention for the pages, because a previous draft gave different pages. The Chamber considers the passages at pages 8, 21, 23, 28, and 40 of the Gotovina-generated transcript, and corresponding to pages 7, 18, 19, 23, 26, and 30 of the English translation of P461, to be sufficiently relevant to warrant a revision by CLSS. I add to this that I have not given the Arkan/Orkans page number in the original, although page 26 is mentioned for the English transcript. I didn't have that page available, but it is to be included in the transcript in the original version. With regards to parts of the transcript that have allegedly been attributed to wrong speakers, the Chamber does not consider the alleged mistakes to be of such a level of relevance to the issues in this case as to warrant a complex further analysis in this regard. The fact that the Gotovina Defence has challenged the accuracy of P461 in this respect is on the record, and the contested parts will be treated with the necessary caution by the Chamber when weighing the evidence. With regard to supposed areas in the translation of the transcript, the Chamber considers the alleged mistakes pointed out by the Gotovina Defence at pages 17 and 38 of the Gotovina-generated transcripts, and corresponding to pages 15 and 29 of the English translation of P461, to be sufficiently relevant to warrant a verification of the translation. To this end, the Gotovina Defence can request CLSS to verify the accuracy of these portions of the transcript as in evidence and get back to the Chamber with the outcome of such verification. The Gotovina Defence shall submit the materials to CLSS for verification by Wednesday, the 27th of January, and shall get back to the Chamber as soon as it receives the results from CLSS. The Chamber, considering the advanced stage of the proceedings, requests CLSS to prioritise the verification of P461. And this concludes the decision of the Chamber on the Gotovina Defence's submissions regarding Exhibit P461. We're running out of tape and time. I have not dealt with all the items, but the tape will run out very soon. But what remain on my list is -- are matters that we can deal with in a still to be scheduled hearing next week. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I did wish to raise an oral motion due to its relative urgency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The -- as the Chamber knows, the European Union issued correspondence to the Chamber yesterday, I believe, or it is dated the 19th of January. We note that it does not appear that the European Union conducted an investigation outside of his own archives to locate the document and it does not record that any effort was made to contact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To keep matters short, Mr. Misetic, there is still an outstanding motion. We asked you to wait for a while until we have received the response. May I assume that the Gotovina Defence wants further action to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. So we make an oral motion for further action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further action in the line of what was earlier requested in your earlier motion when no response had been received at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And in light again of the timing, it is quite urgent for us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I only had a glance at it. We'll further consider the matter but the response has been received. Any further matter? If not, we'll adjourn, sine die, and the Chamber will inform the parties as soon as possible on the scheduling of a session next week. We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.38 p.m.,
